counterfactual_missing_items: No explicit silvery scale, nail changes, or arthritis to make psoriasis unequivocal.
The 2-week painful flare is somewhat shorter than classic chronic plaque psoriasis.
Prednisone use is nonspecific and does not by itself confirm psoriasis.
decisive_items: large, crusted, erythematous plaque on the right chest

Previous treatments included methotrexate, mycophenolate mofetil, cyclosporine, glycopyrrolate, oral antibiotics, topical corticosteroids, topical calcineurin inhibitors, and topical antibiotics, all of which were unsuccessful.
painful area on the right lateral chest
response.rationale: R1 best integrates the large chest plaque with the extensive prior systemic immunomodulatory treatment history and treatment-response/laboratory monitoring context. R4 shares the same plaque phrase but lacks the lupus-specific raw findings such as follicular plugging, scarring, or photosensitivity. R3 is only a generic erythema/plaque overlap without a clear painful refractory course, and R2 has no raw support span.

rejected.why: Shares the same plaque span but would require additional lupus-specific raw features such as follicular plugging, atrophy, or scarring, which are absent.
Only generic plaque morphology overlaps; the right-lateral-chest painful crusted plaque and systemic immunosuppressive failure are atypical for seborrheic dermatitis.
Has no raw support span; prednisone use alone does not support a corticosteroid-induced rosacea-like dermatitis on the chest.
